The Bears are up 20-14 on the Patriots at halftime Thursday thanks mainly to some big plays by wide receiver Luther Burden and a timely interception by linebacker D’Marco Jackson.

They had a chance to go into halftime up 20-7 and getting the ball to begin the third quarter, but squandered that with a sloppy final play. With three seconds left, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye dumped the ball off to running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who ran to the end zone for a 48-yard touchdown.

RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW

Burden is at 130 yards and a touchdown on just four catches, and quarterback Caleb Williams has completed 9 of 16 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown for a 113.3 passer rating.

Jackson ended the Patriots’ best threat at scoring touchdown by picking off a pass from Drake Maye in the end zone.

The Bears jumped to a 10-0 lead by overwhelming the Patriots on both sides of the ball.

The Patriots’ opening drive ended on fourth-and-five at the Bears’ 45-yard line when nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon — Who else? — blitzed to sack Drake Maye. Gordon had three sacks Sunday against the Falcons in his season debut and leads all NFL defensive backs for the season.

Williams followed immediately with a 26-yard pass to Luther Burden to put the Bears in scoring position, and they eventually settled for a 43-yard field goal by Cairo Santos. He and Burden struck again on a 58-yard pass late in the first quarter to set up D’Andre Swift’s four-yard touchdown run.

The Bears had a chance to run away with the game when Williams hit Burden on a 24-yard screen pass for a touchdown and a 20-7 lead with 14 seconds left in the first half, but had an incomprehensible defensive lapse.

Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards, then called timeout at the Bears’ 48-yard line with three seconds left. The Bears were in prevent defense with safeties Dillon Thieneman and Skyler Thomas at the goal line, and Maye threw underneath, seemingly harmlessly, to Stevenson.

The Bears had five players between Stevenson and the end zone at the time he caught the pass, plus defensive back Cam Lewis chasing him from behind, but he weaved through them all the way down the field for a touchdown.

The Bears get the ball to begin the second half.
